title: Vegetarian Crying Tiger (Sua Rong Hai)
subtitle: Recipe Formulation Sheet
scalingPrinciple: The King Oyster Mushroom weight serves as the 100% base. All percentages express the ingredient's relationship to that base mass. Volumes are optimized for the baseline batch size and must be scaled proportionally if batch mass changes.

rows.name: Golden Mountain Soy Sauce
rows.role: Glaze salt profile; distinct Thai notes.

rows.name: Tamarind Paste Concentrate
rows.role: Tart, fruity acid base for the jaew sauce.

rows.name: Vegan Fish Sauce
rows.role: Sharp, salty umami backbone for the jaew.

rows.name: Fresh Lime Juice
rows.role: High-note acidity to finish the sauce.

rows.name: Coconut Palm Sugar (Sauce)
rows.role: Sweet balance for the heavy tamarind.

rows.name: Shallots (Micro-planed)
rows.role: Pungent, sweet aromatic for the jaew.

rows.name: Khao Khua (Toasted Sticky Rice Powder)
rows.role: Vital texturizer; nutty aroma and crunch.

rows.name: Shallots (Ring-sliced)
rows.role: Fresh aromatic component for herb bed.

rows.name: Fresh Mint Leaves
rows.role: Whole leaf herb bed; aromatic contrast.

rows.name: Fresh Cilantro Leaves
rows.role: Whole leaf herb bed; fresh profile.

rows.name: Culantro Leaves (Saw-Tooth)
rows.role: Ultra-fine ribbon slices for herb bed.

mise.label: Aromatic Base
mise.text: Combine coriander roots/stems (B.04) and garlic (B.05) in a heavy stone mortar. Pound until a smooth, uniform paste forms.

mise.label: Substrate Score
mise.text: Trim the woody base of the King Oysters (A.01). Slice vertically into clean 1/2-inch thick planks. Score a tight 1/8-inch deep diamond cross-hatch pattern on both flat faces to bypass surface tension and maximize glaze channels.

mise.label: Herb Bed
mise.text: Wash and spin-dry mint (D.02), cilantro (D.03), and culantro (D.04). Toss whole leaves, culantro ribbons, and sliced shallots (D.01) in a chilled bowl. Store cold.

mise.label: Jaew Base
mise.text: Whisk tamarind (C.01), vegan fish sauce (C.02), lime juice (C.03), and palm sugar (C.04) until fully dissolved. Stir in micro-planed shallots (C.05). Crucial: hold the rice powder and chili flakes back until service.

execution.name: Dry-Weighted Sear
execution.text: Lay the scored mushroom planks completely dry into a blistering hot cast-iron skillet wiped down with the neutral oil (B.06). Apply continuous downward pressure with a heavy pan-weight or metal spatula. This forces out internal air pockets and cooks off natural moisture rapidly, avoiding the classic "chitin sponge" steaming issue. Flip halfway through.

execution.name: Glaze Lacquer Reduction
execution.text: While the steaks finish their sear, heat the pounded garlic/coriander paste, mushroom oyster sauce (B.01), Golden Mountain soy (B.02), and the glaze palm sugar (B.03) in a separate small saucepan. Simmer gently until the sugars reduce into a thick, syrupy lacquer. Pull mushrooms from the iron pan, set them on a wire rack, and paint both sides generously with the hot reduction.

execution.name: Broiler Radiant Flash
execution.text: Transfer the glazed planks directly under a preheated high broiler element. The intense top-down radiant heat will rapidly bubble, caramelize, and fuse the sticky lacquer onto the pre-charred ridges without softening the dense, steak-like core of the mushroom.

qc.target: Dense, chewy, steak-like resistance. Zero flaccid or spongy tissue.
Deeply caramelized amber finish inside the cross-hatch definition. Glossy and bubbling.
Crisp crunch from the late-addition toasted rice powder against the warm, sticky glaze.

sections.title: VI. Iteration & Optimization
sections.intro: Carried forward from the v2.0 Technical Build Sheet, which this formulation supersedes.

items.label: Identified issue:
items.text: Traditional wet-marinating introduces excess external water into a porous ingredient, leading to a steamed, spongy texture when pan-seared.

items.label: Implemented fix:
items.text: Redesigned the sequence to use a dry, weighted pan-press followed by an independent broiler glaze reduction.

items.label: Observation:
items.text: By completely separating the moisture evacuation phase (the dry sear) from the surface caramelization phase (the broiler flash), the classic chitin sponge problem is solved. The glaze adheres to the open cross-hatch channels instead of sliding off into a pool of mushroom water.

directive: Always stir the Khao Khua (C.06) and Prik Bon (C.07) into the nam jim jaew liquid at the absolute last millisecond before slicing the warm steaks. This guarantees the rice powder preserves its maximum crunch.
